primary_frame: Predict employee performance_rating from workplace and experience features (regression)
alternative_frames: Classify employees into performance tiers (high/medium/low) using binned performance_rating
Identify which workplace factors most associate with satisfaction_score
Predict salary_band from employee attributes (multi-class classification)
Cluster employees by work profile to discover latent segments (unsupervised)
required_checks: Test each feature for statistically significant correlation with performance_rating before modeling
Check for multicollinearity among numeric predictors
Verify performance_rating distribution shape and detect outliers
Examine commute_minutes for heavy right skew and potential outliers
Confirm salary_band level frequencies are sufficient for stratified analysis
Run a baseline permutation or null-model test to establish whether any predictive signal exists
framing_risks: No explicit target variable is designated; performance_rating is assumed as target based on column semantics
Features may be independently generated with no genuine predictive relationship to any target (pure noise risk); any detected correlations could be spurious
Dataset has zero nulls and uniformly 800 rows, which is atypical of real HR data and suggests synthetic generation
salary_band is ambiguous: it could be a predictor or an alternative target depending on the business question
No temporal ordering or causal metadata is present, so causal claims from any model would be unjustified
With 8 candidate predictors and 800 rows, multiple-testing and overfitting risks are moderate
